question: Roughly what share of the world's oil goes into making plastics?
answer: About 6%, by a 2016 estimate: roughly what all the world's aircraft use. Most oil is burned as fuel in engines and boilers and vanishes as it is used, while plastic stays in view all day, in every room and every bin.
move: What you see all day is not necessarily what uses the most.
trap: About 30%: plastic is everywhere, so it must take much of the oil.
source: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, The New Plastics Economy, 2016
reference: World Economic Forum, Ellen MacArthur Foundation & McKinsey & Company, The New Plastics Economy: Rethinking the future of plastics, 2016
